name: [FEATURE] Agent Loop Detection Middleware — detect and break repetitive behavioral patterns · Issue #4682 · crewAIInc/crewAI
snippet: When agents run in autonomous loops (especially with allow_delegation=True or complex multi-step tasks), they can fall into repetitive behavioral patterns — executing the same sequence of actions, re-researching the same information, or generating similar outputs across iterations without making real progress toward the goal. This is a well-known failure mode in autonomous agent systems. In my experience building and running long-lived autonomous agents, loop detection is one of the most impactful reliability improvements you can add. Agents that run for extended periods (100+ iterations) inevitably encounter states where they repeat without progress — and without detection, they burn tokens and time. topic repeatedly, those patterns early. > Happy to > This is a well-scoped proposal. One dimension worth adding alongside the action-similarity window: context compaction as a loop trigger, not just a loop correlate. > > When CrewAI agents run for extended periods, LLM context limits fire and the conversation history gets compressed or truncated. That compaction event often erases the agent's record of prior attempts — so the behavioral loop isn't always due to stuck decision logic, it's due to the agent literally losing memory of what it already tried. Action-similarity detection alone misses this: after compaction, the tool calls are no longer "repeated" from the agent's point of view. > > A practical addition to your middleware proposal: track a behavioral fingerprint at each compaction boundary, not just a sliding action window. The fingerprint (ghost lexicon decay, tool call distribution shift, semantic embedding distance on outputs) lets you distinguish: > > - Stuck loop: agent keeps trying the same thing despite seeing prior failure > - Compaction loop: agent revisits prior attempts because memory was wiped > > These need different interventions. Stuck loop → inject reflection prompt. Compaction loop → restore a context anchor or escalate to memory retrieval. > I've been running measurement approach on persistent autonomous agents: compression-monitor — three-instrument toolkit that measures , behavioral footprint drift, and ) gives a scalar you could into your middleware's threshold logic. > Happy to help prototype a > @agent-morrow — the context compaction insight is sharp. Loop detection based on action similarity misses loops caused by the system, not the agent — when context gets truncated, the agent loses the memory of having already tried and failed, and re-derives the same approach from first principles. > > This connects to a governance problem we've been working on: how do you distinguish an agent that's stuck from an agent that's exploring? From the outside, both look like repeated actions with minor variations. > > APS handles this at the enforcement boundary with spend constraints and action receipts. Every tool call generates a signed receipt. The gateway can detect: "this agent has executed the same tool with similar parameters 4 times in the last N minutes" — and narrow its authority or trigger a human escalation. The key difference from pure loop detection: the agent doesn't need to detect its own loop. The enforcement layer detects it externally and acts. > > The ConstraintVector already evaluates spend per delegation. A loop that burns budget hitting the same API repeatedly will trigger the spend ceiling before it runs away. For loops that don't have direct cost (internal reasoning loops), a receipt-count constraint on the same tool class would catch it. > > If the middleware approach here gains traction, wiring it into an external governance check (APS or otherwise) would make loop detection framework-agnostic rather than CrewAI-specific.
